## How to Use This Blind Recognition Checkpoint {#sec-cp03-how-to-use}

Across Part III ([Chapter 09](../chapters/ch09-sam-duality-gsam-trie-bfs.qmd) through [Chapter 14](../chapters/ch14-cdawg-scdawg-suffix-balanced-trees.qmd)), you developed six suffix-structural engines that govern substring equivalence, multi-string aggregation, range-clipped substring queries, and online bi-directional updates:

1. **[Chapter 09 — $\text{SAM}(S) \leftrightarrow \text{ST}(S^R)$ Blumer–Crochemore Duality and 3-Case Trie-BFS Generalized SAM (`广义 SAM`)](../chapters/ch09-sam-duality-gsam-trie-bfs.qmd)**: Translating prefix $\text{LCP}$ queries on $S$ into Link-Tree $\text{LCA}$ queries on $\text{SAM}(S^R)$, eliminating zero-length ghost clones via the 3-case `extend_gsam(p, c)` contract, and constructing multi-string / compressed-Trie automata in strict $O(V|\Sigma|)$ time via **Trie-BFS** to defeat the $\Theta(V^2)$ binary-alphabet Trie-DFS counterexample.
2. **[Chapter 10 — SAM + Persistent Segment Tree Merging on $\text{endpos}$ and Substring Containment Clipping](../chapters/ch10-sam-endpos-segtree-merge.qmd)**: Maintaining every state's occurrence set $\text{endpos}_S(u)$ in $O(N \log N)$ total time and space via non-destructive bottom-up Segment Tree merging, enforcing the exact **Substring Containment Clipping Identity** $\text{endpos}_S(u) \cap [l + L - 1, r] \ne \emptyset$, and jumping intra-state valid lengths via predecessor queries $L_{\text{valid}}(u) = \min(L_{\text{raw}}, e_{\max} - l + 1)$.
3. **[Chapter 11 — Dynamic SAM + Link-Cut Tree (`access` Color-Chain Sweeping) and Intra-State Length Stratification](../chapters/ch11-dynamic-sam-lct-stratification.qmd)**: Maintaining $\mathcal{T}_{\text{link}}$ dynamically under online right-appends (`access(q); splay(q)` before cloning), sweeping right endpoints $r = 1 \dots N$ via LCT `access(pos[r])` so monochrome splay chains telescope into gap-free start-position intervals $[p_{\text{old}} - \text{len}(u_k) + 1, p_{\text{old}} - \text{len}(\text{link}(u_1))]$, and stratifying intra-state lengths ($B_j$ before $A_i$ on ties) for substring implication DAGs.
4. **[Chapter 12 — Linear-Time Induced Sorting (`SA-IS`), Fischer's Induced LCP, and $\text{rk}$-Descent Duality](../chapters/ch12-sais-induced-sorting-lcp.qmd)**: Parsing $S$ into $\le \lfloor N/2 \rfloor$ prefix-free Leftmost $S$-type (LMS) blocks compared by $(S[\cdot], \text{type}(\cdot))$, inducing all $L$-type and $S$-type suffixes in two linear pointer sweeps, inducing `height[2..N]` in $O(N)$ time, and mapping $L/S$ types bijectively to the descent set of $\text{rk}$.
5. **[Chapter 13 — Zero-Tree Virtual Suffix Trees (`后缀树虚树`) and Suffix Tree Dominant Pairs (`启发式合并支配对`)](../chapters/ch13-virtual-suffix-trees-dominant-pairs.qmd)**: Exploiting the 3-way isomorphism $\mathcal{T}_{\text{ST}}(S) \cong \mathcal{T}_{\text{link}}(\text{SAM}(S^R)) \cong \text{Min-Cartesian}(\text{height}[2..N])$, building $O(k \log k)$ Virtual Suffix Trees over arbitrary substrings via adjacent clipped LCEs without an explicit tree, and extracting $\le 2N \log_2 N$ predecessor/successor **Dominant Pairs** $(i^-, i, \ell_u)$ via DSU-on-Tree.
6. **[Chapter 14 — Compact, Persistent & Bi-Directional Suffix Structures: `CDAWG`, `SCDAWG`, and Hash-Free Suffix Balanced Trees (`后缀平衡树`)](../chapters/ch14-cdawg-scdawg-suffix-balanced-trees.qmd)**: Compacting unary right-extension chains into symmetric maximal-repeat vertices ($\overleftarrow{w} = w = \overrightarrow{w}$), eliminating amortized link loops on version trees via `anc_trans[u][c]`, and supporting online encrypted `push_front`/`pop_front` via an $\alpha = 0.75$ Scapegoat Suffix Balanced Tree with 64-bit tags and hash-free BST RMQ LCPs.

::: {.callout-important title="Zero-Spoiler Protocol & Progressive Hints"}
1. **Strict Zero-Spoiler Rule in Visible Statements**: Every problem statement (`CP-III-01` through `CP-III-08`) is written in pure contest form without naming the target chapter (`Ch 09`–`Ch 14`), Online Judge source, or technique (`3-Case GSAM`, `Trie-BFS`, `Persistent Endpos Merge`, `LCT access Sweep`, `SA-IS`, `Virtual Suffix Tree`, `Dominant Pairs`, `Suffix Balanced Tree`).
2. **Diagnose Before Peeking**: Before opening any dropdown on a problem, write down on scratch paper:
   - Which **Part III chapter (`Ch 09`–`Ch 14`)** governs the problem;
   - Which **competing decoy paradigms** must be ruled out, and why;
   - The exact **combinatorial word invariant** and **clipping boundary** required to avoid off-by-one or quadratic blowup traps.
3. **Four-Stage Progressive Unmasking**:
   - **Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Decoy Elimination**: Explains how to identify the governing paradigm and rule out lookalike decoys purely from constraints and query semantics.
   - **Hint 2 — Combinatorial Word Invariant**: States the exact duality, clipping, telescoping, or dominance identity needed for the reduction.
   - **Hint 3 — Algorithmic & Data-Structure Assembly**: Outlines the state representation, preprocessing structures, and complexity target.
   - **Complete Derivation, Complexity Proof & Reference Solution**: Full proof, boundary pitfall audit, and non-standard reference kernel where clarifying.
:::

## 1. Blind Diagnostic Triage Guide: Disambiguating Competing Part III Symptoms {#sec-cp03-triage-guide}

Almost every strategic misdiagnosis in Part III stems from confusing one of two lookalike clusters: **(A) the 3-Way Range Substring Query Decoy Triad (`Ch 10` vs. `Ch 11` vs. `Ch 13`)**, or **(B) the Multi-Branch / Online Direction Decoy Pair (`Ch 09` vs. `Ch 12` vs. `Ch 14`)**.

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Part III 6-Way Blind Triage Flowchart (Open After Reviewing Tables 1.1 & 1.2)"}

```{mermaid}

    Q1 -->|"Range [l, r] or Subset Query on Static S"| R1{"What object is being queried\nor optimized inside S[l..r]?"}
```

### 1.1 Decoy Triad I: Range `[l, r]` Substring Queries (`Ch 10` vs. `Ch 11` vs. `Ch 13`)

When a problem gives $Q$ range queries $[l, r]$ on $S[1..N]$, ask: **what varies inside $[l, r]$?**

| Diagnostic Dimension | `Ch 10` Symptom (Persistent $\text{endpos}$ Merge) | `Ch 11` Symptom (LCT `access` Color-Chain Sweep) | `Ch 13` Symptom (Suffix-Tree Dominant Pairs) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Core Query Object** | **External pattern $T$** (or another specified slice $S[c..d]$) tested for occurrence inside $S[l..r]$, OR nested chain DP over single-witness states. | **All distinct substrings** of $S[l..r]$ simultaneously (counting distinct substrings, length-weighted sums, or range $K$-th distinct substring). | **Pairwise interaction** between two occurrences $l \le a < b \le r$ (e.g., range longest repeated substring $\max_{a < b} \min(r-b+1, \text{LCP}(a,b))$ or range Z-sum). |
| **Why the Other Two Fail** | LCT sweep tracks only the *rightmost* occurrence $\text{last}_r(u)$ of *all* states, which is useless for walking an external pattern $T$; Dominant Pairs only track internal pairs $(a, b)$. | Persistent $\text{endpos}$ merge can query one state $u$ in $O(\log N)$, but $S[l..r]$ touches $\Theta(N)$ SAM states—querying each state separately takes $\Theta(QN \log N)$! | LCT `access` tracks the *first* ($\text{last}_r$) occurrence for distinctness; for repeats or bi-colored pairs $(a, b)$ with $c_a \ne c_b$, you need $\le 2N\log_2 N$ DSU-on-Tree dominant pairs. |
| **Exact Clipping Formula** | Pattern of length $L$ at state $u$ occurs in $S[l..r] \iff \text{endpos}_S(u) \cap [l + L - 1, r] \ne \emptyset$. | Solid chain $C$ with old color $p_{\text{old}}$ covers rightmost start positions $[p_{\text{old}} - L_{\max}(C) + 1, p_{\text{old}} - L_{\min}(C) + 1]$. | Dominant triple $(a, b, \ell_u)$ ($a < b$) contributes $\min(r - b + 1, \ell_u)$: split at $b + \ell_u - 1 \le r$ (value $\ell_u$) vs. $b \le r < b + \ell_u - 1$ (value $r - b + 1$). |

### 1.2 Decoy Triad II: Multi-Branch Trees & Online Directionality (`Ch 09` vs. `Ch 11` vs. `Ch 14`)

When strings grow dynamically or live on a tree, check **which end of the string grows** and **whether the tree is known offline**:

| Diagnostic Dimension | `Ch 09` Symptom (Trie-BFS GSAM) | `Ch 11` Symptom (Online Right-Append LCT-SAM) | `Ch 14` Symptom (Suffix Balanced Tree / Persistent SAM / SCDAWG) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Growth Direction & Topology** | **Offline compressed Trie** $\mathcal{T}$ of $V$ nodes (or unrooted tree with $\le 20$ leaves). | **Online right-append** (`S += c`) to a single string + online pattern occurrence queries. | **Online encrypted `push_front` / `pop_front`**, OR **online version-tree branching** (`append(version_v, c)`), OR **two-ended `push_front` + `push_back`**. |
| **Fatal Misdiagnosis** | Running **Trie-DFS** instead of **Trie-BFS** ($\Theta(V^2)$ Case-3 link walks on $\{\texttt{a}^k\texttt{b}\}$), or resetting `last = 1` with single-string `extend` (zero-length ghost clones). | Copying `val[clone] = val[q]` during an LCT split without calling `access(q); splay(q);` first (leaves lazy $+1$ path tags stranded above $q$). | Trying to run Suffix Balanced Tree on `push_back(c)` (appending `'b'` to `"aa"` flips suffix order `"a" < "aa"` to `"aab" < "ab"`!), or running amortized SAM link walks on a star version tree ($\Theta(N^2)$). |

## 2. Unspoiled Blind Checkpoint Problems (`CP-III-01`–`CP-III-08`) {#sec-cp03-problems}

---

### Problem `CP-III-01` — All-Path Substring Census on a Low-Leaf Tree

> **Statement**: You are given an unrooted tree $T = (V, E)$ with $N$ vertices ($1 \le N \le 10^5$), where each vertex $u \in V$ carries a character label $c_u \in \{1, 2, \dots, |\Sigma|\}$ ($1 \le |\Sigma| \le 10$). It is guaranteed that the tree $T$ has **at most $L \le 20$ leaves** (vertices of degree $1$).
>
> Every simple path $(u_1, u_2, \dots, u_k)$ in $T$ spells a string $c_{u_1} c_{u_2} \cdots c_{u_k}$ of length $k$. Compute the total number of **distinct** non-empty strings that can be spelled by simple paths in $T$.
>
> **Constraints**: $1 \le N \le 10^5$, $1 \le |\Sigma| \le 10$, number of degree-$1$ vertices $L \le 20$, time limit $1.5\text{ s}$, memory limit $512\text{ MB}$.

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Decoy Elimination"}
- **Decoy Elimination**: This is *not* an upward-tree suffix sorting problem (`Ch 12`), where paths only go toward a single fixed root, nor is it an online version-tree query problem (`Ch 14`). We must count distinct strings across **all** directed simple paths $u \to v$ in an unrooted tree.
- **Diagnostic Signal**: Look at the constraint $L \le 20$ leaves! Any directed simple path $u \to v$ in a tree can be extended backward from $u$ until it starts at some leaf $r$ of $T$. Therefore, every simple-path string $u \to v$ is a **substring** (in fact, a prefix of a root-to-node path, and conversely every substring of a leaf-rooted path is a simple path!) of the tree $T$ when rooted at one of its $L \le 20$ leaves!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 2 — Combinatorial Word Invariant"}
Root the tree $T$ independently at each of the $L \le 20$ leaves $r_1, \dots, r_L$. Every directed simple path $u \to v$ in $T$ can be extended backward from $u$ to some leaf $r_i$, making $u \to v$ a suffix of the root-to-$v$ path in $T_{r_i}$. Conversely, every substring of a root-to-node path in $T_{r_i}$ is a simple path in $T$. Thus the set of **all simple-path strings** in $T$ is *identical* to the set of **all substrings of root-to-node paths** across the $L$ leaf-rooted trees $T_{r_1}, \dots, T_{r_L}$!

When inserting $L$ trees of total vertex count $\le L \cdot N \le 2 \times 10^6$ into a single automaton that merges shared prefixes/substrings without sentinel bloat, which Part III invariant prevents zero-length ghost states and avoids the $\Theta(V^2)$ traversal trap?
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 3 — Algorithmic & Data-Structure Assembly"}
1. Identify all leaves $r_1, \dots, r_L$ ($\text{deg}(r) = 1$, or $N = 1$).
2. Either merge the $L$ leaf-rooted trees into a single compressed Trie of size $V \le L N$ and run **Trie-BFS** with the **3-Case `extend_gsam(p, c)`** routine (`Ch 09`), OR run a BFS from each leaf $r_i$ passing `sam_node[u] = extend_gsam(sam_node[parent], c_u)` along tree edges $parent \to u$ in increasing order of depth.
3. Once all $L$ leaf-rooted trees are inserted into the shared automaton, every state $u > 1$ represents $\text{len}(u) - \text{len}(\text{link}(u))$ distinct simple-path strings. Sum $\sum_{u > 1} (\text{len}(u) - \text{len}(\text{link}(u)))$ in $O(L N |\Sigma|)$ time.
::::

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Complete Derivation, Complexity Proof & Reference Solution — CP-III-01"}

- **Problem Source**: `[ZJOI2015] 诸神眷顾的幻想乡 (Fantasy乡 Loved by the Gods)` (`Luogu P3346` / `LOJ 2130`, `W2A-12`).
- **Target Chapter & Technique ID**: **[Chapter 09](../chapters/ch09-sam-duality-gsam-trie-bfs.qmd) (`T-2A-01`: 3-Case Generalized SAM & Trie-BFS Construction)**.
- **Proof of Leaf-Rooted Completeness**:
  Let $(u_1, u_2, \dots, u_k)$ be any simple path in $T$. Extend the path backward from $u_1$ away from $u_2$ until it reaches a leaf $r_i$. In the tree $T_{r_i}$ rooted at $r_i$, $(u_1, \dots, u_k)$ is a contiguous sub-path of the root-to-$u_k$ path $r_i \rightsquigarrow u_1 \to \dots \to u_k$, so its label is a suffix of the root-to-$u_k$ string in $T_{r_i}$. Conversely, every suffix of a root-to-$v$ string in $T_{r_i}$ corresponds to a simple path in $T$. Thus the set of distinct simple-path strings in $T$ equals the set of distinct substrings of the $L$ leaf-rooted Tries $T_{r_1}, \dots, T_{r_L}$.

- **Why 3-Case `extend_gsam` & BFS Are Mandatory (`Boundary Pitfall Audit`)**:
  1. **Tree Branching (`sam_node[parent]`)**: When a tree vertex $p$ has multiple children $v_1, v_2$ with the *same* character $c_{v_1} = c_{v_2} = c$, after processing $v_1$, $\delta(\text{sam\_node}[p], c)$ is already non-zero! Calling single-string `extend` on $v_2$ creates a zero-length ghost clone (`Counterexample 9.3` of `Ch 09`). The 3-case `extend_gsam(sam_node[p], c)` hits Case 2 ($\text{len}(q) = \text{len}(p) + 1$) and returns $q$ in $O(1)$ time (or Case 3 if a longer path from an earlier leaf already set $\delta(p, c)$).
  2. **Defeating the $\Theta(V^2)$ Trie-DFS Trap (`Theorem 9.4`)**: Merging the $L$ leaf-rooted trees into a single Trie of $V \le L N$ vertices and traversing it in **BFS** order processes vertices in non-decreasing depth $\text{len}(p)$, guaranteeing $O(V |\Sigma|) = O(L N |\Sigma|)$ total time and at most $2 L N$ states.
- **Complexity**: $O(L N |\Sigma|)$ time and $O(L N |\Sigma|)$ space ($\le 4 \times 10^6$ states).
::::

### Problem `CP-III-02` — Decreasing-Length Disjoint Substring Chain

> **Statement**: You are given a string $S[1..N]$ of lowercase English letters ($1 \le N \le 5 \times 10^5$). Find the maximum positive integer $k$ such that there exist $k$ **non-overlapping** substrings $t_1, t_2, \dots, t_k$ appearing from left to right in $S$ ($t_i = S[l_i..r_i]$ with $1 \le l_1 \le r_1 < l_2 \le r_2 < \dots < l_k \le r_k \le N$) satisfying:
>
> 1. $|t_i| = k - i + 1$ for every $i \in \{1, 2, \dots, k\}$ (so $|t_1| = k, |t_2| = k-1, \dots, |t_k| = 1$);
> 2. For every $i \in \{1, 2, \dots, k-1\}$, $t_{i+1}$ is a **substring** of $t_i$.
>
> **Constraints**: $1 \le N \le 5 \times 10^5$, $|\Sigma| = 26$, time limit $5.0\text{ s}$, memory limit $512\text{ MB}$.

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Decoy Elimination"}
- **Decoy Elimination**: In `CF 700E` (`Cool Slogans`, `Ch 10`), $s_{i-1}$ must occur twice inside $s_i$, and substring lengths can jump by arbitrary amounts along the Link Tree. Here, $|t_i| = k - i + 1$ decreases by **exactly $1$** at each step, and the chosen occurrences $S[l_1..r_1], \dots, S[l_k..r_k]$ must be **disjoint in position** ($r_i < l_{i+1}$).
- **Diagnostic Signal**: Since $|t_i| = |t_{i+1}| + 1$ and $t_{i+1}$ is a substring of $t_i$, $t_{i+1}$ must be **either the prefix $t_i[1..|t_i|-1]$ or the suffix $t_i[2..|t_i|]$**! Furthermore, let $dp[i]$ be the maximum chain length $L$ starting with $t_1 = S[i .. i + L - 1]$. If $S[i .. i + L - 1]$ starts a valid chain of length $L$, then dropping its first character $S[i]$ leaves $S[i + 1 .. i + L - 1]$, which still contains $t_2$ (of length $L - 1$, or its suffix of length $L - 2$) and starts a valid chain of length $\ge L - 1$ at $i + 1$!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 2 — Combinatorial Word Invariant"}
From the left-truncation observation above, $dp[i]$ satisfies the **1-Lipchitz Right-to-Left Monotonicity Invariant**:
$$dp[i] \le dp[i + 1] + 1 \qquad \forall i \in \{1, \dots, N - 1\}.$$
Consequently, if we sweep $i$ from $N$ down to $1$, starting our candidate length at $L = dp[i + 1] + 1$ and decrementing $L$ until $L$ is valid at $i$:

1. The pointer $i + L$ (the minimum allowed starting position $j \ge i + L$ of the non-overlapping next piece $t_2 = S[j .. j + L - 2]$) **decreases monotonically** across the entire sweep ($O(N)$ decrements in total)!
2. A candidate length $L$ is valid at index $i$ if and only if there exists $j \ge i + L$ with $dp[j] \ge L - 1$ such that $S[j .. j + L - 2]$ equals **either** $S[i .. i + L - 2]$ **or** $S[i + 1 .. i + L - 1]$.
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 3 — Algorithmic & Data-Structure Assembly"}
1. Build $\text{SAM}(S^R)$ so that its Link Tree $\mathcal{T}_{\text{link}}(\text{SAM}(S^R)) \cong \text{ST}(S)$ groups substrings of $S$ by right-extension / common **prefix** (`Ch 09` Blumer–Crochemore Duality). Compute the Euler-tour interval $[\text{dfn}[u], \text{out}[u]]$ of every state $u$ on $\mathcal{T}_{\text{link}}(\text{SAM}(S^R))$ (or equivalently use the Suffix Array interval on $\text{SA}_S$).
2. A suffix starting at $j$ has $S[i .. i + L - 2]$ as a prefix of length $L - 1$ iff the terminal state $\text{pos}[j]$ lies in the Link-Tree **subtree** of the ancestor $u_1$ of $\text{pos}[i]$ at length $L - 1$ ($\text{len}(\text{link}(u_1)) < L - 1 \le \text{len}(u_1)$). Similarly, $S[j .. j + L - 2] = S[i + 1 .. i + L - 1]$ iff $\text{pos}[j]$ lies in the subtree of the ancestor $u_2$ of $\text{pos}[i+1]$ at length $L - 1$.
3. Sweep $i = N \dots 1$. Whenever $L$ is decremented, the threshold $j = i + L$ moves left by $1$: insert $dp[j]$ into a Range-Max Segment Tree at leaf $\text{dfn}[\text{pos}[j]]$. Check $L$ in $O(\log N)$ time by querying whether the subtree of $u_1$ or $u_2$ has $\max dp \ge L - 1$. Total time: $O(N \log N)$.
::::

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Complete Derivation, Complexity Proof & Reference Solution — CP-III-02"}

- **Problem Source**: Codeforces 1063F — *String Journey* (`W2A-27` / `W2B-40`).
- **Target Chapter & Technique ID**: **[Chapter 09](../chapters/ch09-sam-duality-gsam-trie-bfs.qmd) & [Chapter 10](../chapters/ch10-sam-endpos-segtree-merge.qmd) (`T-2A-01` / `T-2A-03`: Reversed-SAM Link-Tree Locus Lifting + Two-Pointer Non-Overlapping Subtree RMQ)**.
- **Why $\text{len}(u)$ Needs No Further Clipping Inside $u$'s Subtree**:
  On $\mathcal{T}_{\text{link}}(\text{SAM}(S^R)) \cong \text{ST}(S)$, let $u_1$ be the unique ancestor of $\text{pos}_{S^R}[N - i + 1]$ satisfying $\text{len}(\text{link}(u_1)) < L - 1 \le \text{len}(u_1)$. Every suffix leaf $\text{pos}_{S^R}[N - j + 1]$ in the Link-Tree subtree of $u_1$ shares a common prefix with $S[i..N]$ of length at least $\text{len}(u_1) \ge L - 1$, so $S[j .. j + L - 2] = S[i .. i + L - 2]$ holds identically for every $j$ in $u_1$'s subtree!

- **Incremental Locus Maintenance in $O(1)$ per Decrement**:
  Even the binary lifting to find $u_1$ and $u_2$ can be reduced from $O(\log N)$ to $O(1)$ amortized time: as $L$ decrements, if $L - 1 \le \text{len}(\text{link}(u_1))$, simply step $u_1 \leftarrow \text{link}(u_1)$!

- **Boundary Pitfall Audit**:
  - **Premature Insertion into the Segment Tree**: Never insert $dp[j]$ into the Segment Tree before the pointer $i + L$ reaches $j$. If $dp[j]$ is active while $j < i + L$, then $t_1 = S[i .. i + L - 1]$ and $t_2 = S[j .. j + L - 2]$ overlap!
- **Complexity**: $O(N \log N)$ time and $O(N)$ space.
::::

### Problem `CP-III-03` — First-Occurrence Naïve Matcher Comparison Count

> **Statement**: You are given a fixed text string $S[1..N]$ of digits ($1 \le N \le 10^5$) and $Q$ query patterns $P_1, P_2, \dots, P_Q$ ($1 \le Q \le 10^5, \sum_{q=1}^Q |P_q| \le 10^5$).
>
> For a query pattern $P[1..M]$, consider a naïve string matcher that tests starting positions $i = 1, 2, \dots, N$ in increasing order. At each starting position $i$, it compares $P[1], P[2], \dots$ against $S[i], S[i+1], \dots$ one character at a time from left to right until **either**:
>
> - A mismatch occurs (or the end of $S$ is reached at $i + k - 1 = N$ before $k = M$), taking $\text{LCP}(P, S[i..N]) + 1$ character comparisons (or $\text{LCP}(P, S[i..N])$ if $i + \text{LCP}(P, S[i..N]) - 1 = N$, i.e., $S[i..N]$ is a proper prefix of $P$ and runs out of characters without a mismatching character); **or**
> - All $M$ characters match ($S[i..i+M-1] = P$), taking $M$ character comparisons, at which point the matcher **halts immediately** and does not inspect any $i' > i$.
>
> For each query $P_q$, output the total number of character comparisons performed by the naïve matcher.
>
> **Constraints**: $1 \le N, Q \le 10^5$, $\sum_{q=1}^Q |P_q| \le 10^5$, $|\Sigma| = 10$, time limit $1.5\text{ s}$, memory limit $256\text{ MB}$.

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Decoy Elimination"}
- **Decoy Elimination (Decoy Triad I)**: We are querying an **external pattern $P_q$** against prefixes/substrings of $S$ up to the first occurrence of $P_q$ in $S$. Neither LCT color-chain sweeping (`Ch 11`, which aggregates all distinct substrings of $S[l..r]$) nor Suffix-Tree Dominant Pairs (`Ch 13`, which optimizes internal suffix pairs $(a, b)$ of $S$) applies to an external pattern $P_q$!
- **Diagnostic Signal**: Let $i_0$ be the starting index of the **first** occurrence of $P$ in $S$ (or $i_0 = N$ if $P$ never occurs in $S$). Apart from the baseline $1$ mismatch comparison per tested index $i \le i_0$ (adjusted for suffixes $S[i..N]$ that are proper prefixes of $P$, or the full match at $i_0$), the core sum we must compute is:
  $$\sum_{i=1}^{i_0} \text{LCP}(P, S[i..N]).$$
  How can you rewrite $\sum_{i=1}^{i_0} \text{LCP}(P, S[i..N])$ in terms of the **prefixes $P[1..k]$** ($1 \le k \le M$) of $P$?
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 2 — Combinatorial Word Invariant"}
By double counting (expressing $\text{LCP}(P, S[i..N]) = \sum_{k=1}^M [P[1..k] \text{ occurs at start } i]$):
$$\sum_{i=1}^{i_0} \text{LCP}(P, S[i..N]) \;=\; \sum_{k=1}^{M} \bigl|\{ i \in [1, i_0] \mid S[i .. i + k - 1] = P[1..k] \}\bigr|.$$
Now translate the starting-position condition $i \in [1, i_0]$ into a **right-endpoint (`endpos`) clipping condition** (`Ch 10` `Theorem 10.1`)! An occurrence of $P[1..k]$ starting at $i$ ends at $e = i + k - 1$. Therefore:
$$1 \le i \le i_0 \iff k \le e \le i_0 + k - 1 \iff e \in [1, \, i_0 + k - 1]!$$
And how do we find $i_0$ itself? If $P[1..M]$ reaches state $u_M$ in $\text{SAM}(S)$, its earliest ending position in $S$ is $e_{\min} = \min \text{endpos}_S(u_M)$, giving $i_0 = e_{\min} - M + 1$!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 3 — Algorithmic & Data-Structure Assembly"}
1. Build $\text{SAM}(S)$ and run **Persistent Bottom-Up Segment Tree Merging** (`Ch 10`) on $\mathcal{T}_{\text{link}}$ so that $\text{rt}[u]$ stores the indicator set $\text{endpos}_S(u) \subseteq [1, N]$ with range-sum and $\min$-element queries.
2. For a query $P[1..M]$, walk $P$ on $\text{SAM}(S)$ from root $1$, recording the state $u_k$ reached by each prefix $P[1..k]$ ($1 \le k \le k_{\max}$ before any transition $\delta(u_k, P[k+1]) = 0$).
3. Determine $i_0$:
   - If $k_{\max} = M$, query the minimum element $e_{\min}$ in $\text{rt}[u_M]$, set $i_0 = e_{\min} - M + 1$, and set the baseline mismatch comparisons to $i_0 - 1$ (since $i = i_0$ halts on full match without an extra mismatch comparison, and no $i < i_0$ can reach the end of $S$ as a proper prefix of $P$ because $i_0 + M - 1 = e_{\min} \le N$).
   - If $k_{\max} < M$, $P$ never occurs in $S$, so $i_0 = N$. How many starting indices $i$ hit the right end $N$ of $S$ as a proper prefix of $P$ without a mismatching character? Exactly those $k \in [1, k_{\max}]$ where $N \in \text{endpos}_S(u_k)$! Each such $k$ saves $1$ comparison from the baseline $N$.
4. Add $\sum_{k=1}^{k_{\max}} \text{query\_count}(\text{rt}[u_k], 1, i_0 + k - 1)$ in $O(|P| \log N)$ time.
::::

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Complete Derivation, Complexity Proof & Reference Solution — CP-III-03"}

- **Problem Source & Decoy Cluster**: `[BZOJ 3413] 匹配 (Matching)` (`W2A-29`, Decoy Triad I · Part 1).
- **Target Chapter & Technique ID**: **[Chapter 10](../chapters/ch10-sam-endpos-segtree-merge.qmd) (`T-2A-03`: SAM + Persistent Segment Tree Merging on $\text{endpos}_S$ with Prefix-Shifted Boundary Clipping)**.
- **Derivation of the Exact Comparison Identity**:
  At starting index $i$, let $\ell_i = \text{LCP}(P, S[i..N])$.

  - If $P$ occurs in $S$, let $i_0 = \min\{i \mid S[i..i+M-1] = P\} = e_{\min} - M + 1$. For every $i < i_0$, we have $\ell_i < M$ and $i + \ell_i \le i_0 - 1 + M = e_{\min} \le N$, so the matcher always compares the mismatching character $S[i + \ell_i] \ne P[\ell_i + 1]$ (cost $\ell_i + 1$). At $i = i_0$, the matcher compares $M = \ell_{i_0}$ characters and halts (cost $\ell_{i_0}$). Summing over $i = 1 \dots i_0$ gives:
    $$\text{Ans} = (i_0 - 1) + \sum_{i=1}^{i_0} \ell_i = (e_{\min} - M) + \sum_{k=1}^M \bigl|\text{endpos}_S(u_k) \cap [1, \, e_{\min} - M + k]\bigr|.$$

  - If $P$ does not occur in $S$, the matcher tests all $i \in [1, N]$. At index $i$, it performs $\ell_i + 1$ comparisons *unless* $i + \ell_i - 1 = N$ (meaning $S[i..N] = P[1..\ell_i]$ hits the end of $S$, which happens iff $\ell_i = N - i + 1 \ge 1 \iff N \in \text{endpos}_S(u_k)$ for $k = N - i + 1 \le k_{\max}$). Thus:
    $$\text{Ans} = N + \sum_{k=1}^{k_{\max}} \Bigl(\bigl|\text{endpos}_S(u_k) \cap [1, N]\bigr| - [N \in \text{endpos}_S(u_k)]\Bigr) = N + \sum_{k=1}^{k_{\max}} \bigl|\text{endpos}_S(u_k) \cap [1, N - 1]\bigr|!$$
    Notice the remarkable simplification when $P$ does not occur in $S$: subtracting $[N \in \text{endpos}_S(u_k)]$ is **identical to querying $\text{endpos}_S(u_k) \cap [1, N - 1]$**!

- **Boundary Pitfall Audit**:
  - **Querying $[1, e_{\min}]$ Instead of $[1, e_{\min} - M + k]$**: An occurrence of $P[1..k]$ starting at $i \le i_0 = e_{\min} - M + 1$ ends at $e = i + k - 1 \le e_{\min} - M + k$. Querying $[1, e_{\min}]$ falsely counts occurrences of $P[1..k]$ that start at $i \in (i_0, e_{\min} - k + 1]$ *after* the matcher has already halted!
- **Complexity**: $O((N + \sum |P_q|) \log N)$ time and $O(N \log N)$ space.
::::

### Problem `CP-III-04` — Dynamic Left-Endpoint $\times$ Right-Endpoint Substring Weight Bilinear Form

> **Statement**: You are given a string $S[1..N]$ of length $N$ ($1 \le N \le 5 \times 10^5$), a static right-endpoint weight array $w_R[1..N]$, and an initial left-endpoint weight array $w_L[1..N]$.
>
> Every distinct non-empty substring $u$ of $S$ has a total left-endpoint weight $W_L(u) = \sum_{(l, r) : S[l..r] = u} w_L[l]$ and a total right-endpoint weight $W_R(u) = \sum_{(l, r) : S[l..r] = u} w_R[r]$, and the global score of $S$ is defined over all **distinct** non-empty substrings $u$ of $S$ as:
> $$\Phi(w_L) \;=\; \sum_{u \text{ distinct in } S} |u| \cdot W_L(u) \cdot W_R(u) \;=\; \sum_{u \text{ distinct in } S} |u| \left(\sum_{S[l..r]=u} w_L[l]\right)\left(\sum_{S[l'..r']=u} w_R[r']\right) \pmod{2^{64}}.$$
> You must process $Q$ online point updates ($1 \le Q \le 5 \times 10^5$). In each update, you are given $(x, \Delta)$ which modifies $w_L[x] \leftarrow w_L[x] + \Delta$. Output the initial value of $\Phi(w_L)$ and its updated value after each of the $Q$ modifications.
>
> **Constraints**: $1 \le N, Q \le 5 \times 10^5$, $|\Sigma| = 26$, arithmetic modulo $2^{64}$ (`uint64_t`), time limit $2.0\text{ s}$, memory limit $512\text{ MB}$.

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Decoy Elimination"}
- **Decoy Elimination**: There are up to $\binom{N+1}{2} = \Theta(N^2)$ distinct substrings $u$, and modifying a single $w_L[x]$ changes $W_L(u)$ for all $N - x + 1$ substrings $u = S[x..r]$ starting at $x$. We cannot iterate over $r \in [x, N]$ per query.
- **Diagnostic Signal**: By linearity over $w_L[x]$, $\Phi(w_L)$ is a **linear form** in the array $w_L[1..N]$:
  $$\Phi(w_L) = \sum_{x=1}^N C[x] \cdot w_L[x],$$
  where the coefficient $C[x]$ of $w_L[x]$ is static (since $S$ and $w_R[1..N]$ never change!). If we can precompute the entire coefficient array $C[1..N]$ in $O(N)$ time, then each point update $w_L[x] \mathrel{+}= \Delta$ updates $\Phi \mathrel{+}= \Delta \cdot C[x]$ in **$O(1)$ time**!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 2 — Combinatorial Word Invariant"}
**Dual SAM / Suffix Tree Factorization**: What is the coefficient $C[x]$ of $w_L[x]$? Every occurrence starting at $x$ is a prefix $S[x..r]$ of the suffix $S[x..N]$ (of length $L = r - x + 1$). Thus:
$$C[x] \;=\; \sum_{r=x}^N (r - x + 1) \cdot W_R(S[x..r]).$$
Why is $W_R(S[x..r])$ awkward on $\text{SAM}(S)$ when $x$ is fixed and $r$ varies, yet effortless when viewed through **Blumer–Crochemore Reversal Duality (`Ch 09` `Theorem 9.2`)**?

1. On **forward $\text{SAM}(S)$**, all strings $w \in E_S(v)$ share the exact same right-endpoint occurrence set $\text{endpos}_S(v)$, so $W_R(w) = W_R(v) = \sum_{r' \in \text{endpos}_S(v)} w_R[r']$ is a constant per state $v \in \text{SAM}(S)$!
2. Moreover, for a representative right endpoint $e_v = \text{pos}_S(v)$ of state $v \in \text{SAM}(S)$, the strings $w \in E_S(v)$ have lengths $L \in [\text{len}(\text{link}(v)) + 1, \, \text{len}(v)]$. However, $W_L(w)$ sums $w_L[l]$ over **all** occurrences $l \in \text{startpos}_S(w)$, not just $e_v - L + 1$!
3. Flip the duality: on **reversed $\text{SAM}(S^R)$** ($\mathcal{T}_{\text{link}}(\text{SAM}(S^R)) \cong \text{ST}(S)$), all strings $w \in E_{S^R}(\tilde{u})$ share the exact same **starting-position set** $\text{startpos}_S(\tilde{u})$, so $W_L(w) = W_L(\tilde{u}) = \sum_{l \in \text{startpos}_S(\tilde{u})} w_L[l]$ is constant across the entire state $\tilde{u} \in \text{SAM}(S^R)$!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 3 — Algorithmic & Data-Structure Assembly"}
1. Build **forward $\text{SAM}(S)$** and compute $W_R(v) = \sum_{r' \in \text{endpos}_S(v)} w_R[r']$ bottom-up on $\mathcal{T}_{\text{link}}(\text{SAM}(S))$ in $O(N)$ time.
2. For each state $v \in \text{SAM}(S)$, pick one representative right endpoint $e_v = \text{pos}_S(v)$. As the substring length $L$ varies over $[\text{len}(\text{link}(v)) + 1, \, \text{len}(v)]$, the representative occurrence $S[e_v - L + 1 .. e_v]$ has fixed right endpoint $e_v$ and **contiguous starting positions** $l = e_v - L + 1 \in [e_v - \text{len}(v) + 1, \, e_v - \text{len}(\text{link}(v))]$.
3. Symmetrically, on **reversed $\text{SAM}(S^R)$**, each state $\tilde{u}$ has one representative starting position $s_{\tilde{u}}$ and covers a contiguous interval of right endpoints $r = s_{\tilde{u}} + L - 1$. Or even simpler: for each state $v \in \text{SAM}(S)$, every occurrence of a string of length $L \in [\text{len}(\text{link}(v)) + 1, \text{len}(v)]$ in $E_S(v)$ is obtained by propagating a linear polynomial weight $L \cdot W_R(v)$ along the contiguous start-position interval $[e_v - \text{len}(v) + 1, \, e_v - \text{len}(\text{link}(v))]$ on $\mathcal{T}_{\text{link}}(\text{SAM}(S^R))$!
4. Using a 1D difference array of linear polynomials $A \cdot l + B$ along the representative suffixes of $\text{SAM}(S^R)$ followed by a single top-down pushdown on $\mathcal{T}_{\text{link}}(\text{SAM}(S^R))$, compute all $C[1..N]$ in **$O(N)$ time** and answer each query in **$O(1)$ time**!
::::

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Complete Derivation, Complexity Proof & Reference Solution — CP-III-04"}

- **Problem Source**: UOJ 577 — *打击复读 (Stop Repeating)* (`W2A-38`).
- **Target Chapter & Technique ID**: **[Chapter 09](../chapters/ch09-sam-duality-gsam-trie-bfs.qmd) & [Chapter 11](../chapters/ch11-dynamic-sam-lct-stratification.qmd) (`T-2A-01` / `T-2A-04`: Bidirectional $\text{SAM}(S) \leftrightarrow \text{SAM}(S^R)$ Interval Factorization)**.
- **Exact Derivation of the $O(N)$ Dual-Automaton Pushdown**:
  1. **Step 1 — Right-Weight Aggregation on $\text{SAM}(S)$**:
     In $\text{SAM}(S)$, every state $v > 1$ bundles lengths $L \in [L_{\min}(v), L_{\max}(v)] = [\text{len}(\text{link}_S(v)) + 1, \text{len}_S(v)]$ that all share the identical right-endpoint weight sum $W_R(v) = \sum_{r \in \text{endpos}_S(v)} w_R[r]$, computed in $O(N)$ time via a bottom-up sum on $\mathcal{T}_{\text{link}}(\text{SAM}(S))$.

  2. **Step 2 — Left-Weight Factorization via Representative End-Positions**:
     For any string $u \in E_S(v)$ of length $L = |u|$, every occurrence of $u$ in $S$ has right endpoint $r \in \text{endpos}_S(v)$ and left endpoint $l = r - L + 1$, so its left-endpoint weight sum is:
     $$\boxed{W_L(u) \;=\; \sum_{r \in \text{endpos}_S(v)} w_L[r - L + 1].}$$
     Symmetrically, on **reversed $\text{SAM}(S^R)$** ($\mathcal{T}_{\text{link}}(\text{SAM}(S^R)) \cong \text{ST}(S)$), every state $\tilde{u} > 1$ bundles strings $u \in E_{S^R}(\tilde{u})$ of lengths $L \in [L_{\min}(\tilde{u}), L_{\max}(\tilde{u})]$ that share the exact same starting-position set $\text{startpos}_S(\tilde{u})$, so $W_L(\tilde{u}) = \sum_{x \in \text{startpos}_S(\tilde{u})} w_L[x]$ is constant across $\tilde{u}$, while for a single representative right endpoint $e_v = \text{pos}_S(v)$ on $\text{SAM}(S)$, the substrings $S[e_v - L + 1 .. e_v]$ ($L \in [L_{\min}(v), L_{\max}(v)]$) have contiguous starting positions $l = e_v - L + 1 \in [e_v - L_{\max}(v) + 1, \, e_v - L_{\min}(v) + 1]$ and right-weight $L \cdot W_R(v) = (e_v + 1 - l) W_R(v)$.

  3. **Step 3 — 1D Polynomial Difference Array + Link-Tree Pushdown**:
     For each state $\tilde{u} \in \text{SAM}(S^R)$ with representative starting position $s_{\tilde{u}}$, let $K(\tilde{u}) = \sum_{L = L_{\min}(\tilde{u})}^{L_{\max}(\tilde{u})} L \cdot W_R(S[s_{\tilde{u}} .. s_{\tilde{u}} + L - 1])$. Accumulating $K(\tilde{u})$ via 1D difference arrays and pushing $K(\tilde{u})$ top-down along $\mathcal{T}_{\text{link}}(\text{SAM}(S^R))$ yields all coefficients $C[x] = \sum_{\tilde{u} \text{ anc of } \text{node}_{S^R}(x)} K(\tilde{u})$ in $O(N)$ total time!

- **Boundary Pitfall Audit**:
  - **Index Inversion Between $S$ and $S^R$**: When mapping a substring $S[l..r]$ of length $L = r - l + 1$ to $\text{SAM}(S^R)$, its reversed counterpart ends at $N - l + 1$ in $S^R$, and its starting index in $S$ is $l = e_v - L + 1$. Reversing the sign of $l$ in the linear polynomial $(e_v + 1 - l) W_R(v)$ corrupts the difference-array coefficients.
- **Complexity**: $O(N)$ preprocessing time, $O(1)$ time per query, $O(N)$ space.
::::

### Problem `CP-III-05` — Range $K$-th Lexicographical Distinct Substring

> **Statement**: You are given a string $S[1..N]$ of lowercase letters ($1 \le N \le 10^5$) and $Q$ queries ($1 \le Q \le 10^5$). Each query provides three integers $(l_q, r_q, K_q)$ ($1 \le l_q \le r_q \le N, 1 \le K_q \le \binom{r_q - l_q + 2}{2}$).
>
> Consider the set $\mathcal{D}(l_q, r_q)$ of all **distinct** non-empty substrings occurring inside $S[l_q..r_q]$, sorted in strictly increasing lexicographical order $w_1 <_{\text{lex}} w_2 <_{\text{lex}} \cdots <_{\text{lex}} w_m$. If $K_q > |\mathcal{D}(l_q, r_q)|$, output `-1`; otherwise, output a pair of indices $(a, b)$ ($l_q \le a \le b \le r_q$) such that $S[a..b] = w_{K_q}$.
>
> **Constraints**: $1 \le N, Q \le 10^5$, $|\Sigma| = 26$, time limit $3.0\text{ s}$, memory limit $512\text{ MB}$.

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Decoy Elimination"}
- **Decoy Elimination (Decoy Triad I)**: Unlike `CP-III-03` (which matches one external pattern $P_q$ via `Ch 10` Persistent $\text{endpos}$ Merge), this query ranks across **all distinct substrings** occurring inside $S[l_q..r_q]$. Why is `Ch 11`'s offline right-endpoint sweep (`r = 1 .. N`) the natural starting point, and what additional structure is needed to navigate **lexicographical order** instead of just counting $|\mathcal{D}(l_q, r_q)|$?
- **Diagnostic Signal**: Instead of the SAM transition DAG (where paths split and re-merge), view $\mathcal{D}(l_q, r_q)$ on the **Suffix Tree $\mathcal{T}_{\text{ST}}(S) \cong \mathcal{T}_{\text{link}}(\text{SAM}(S^R))$** (`Ch 09` / `Ch 13`)! On $\mathcal{T}_{\text{ST}}(S)$, the lexicographical order of **all** distinct substrings of $S$ is simply the **preorder DFS traversal** of $\mathcal{T}_{\text{ST}}(S)$ (ordering outgoing edges at each node alphabetically)!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 2 — Combinatorial Word Invariant"}
**Reversed-Direction Sweep on $\mathcal{T}_{\text{ST}}(S)$**: Let us combine $\mathcal{T}_{\text{ST}}(S) \cong \mathcal{T}_{\text{link}}(\text{SAM}(S^R))$ with `Ch 11`'s **LCT `access` Color-Chain Sweeping**!

1. On $\mathcal{T}_{\text{ST}}(S)$, each node $u > 1$ represents prefixes of $S[i..N]$ of lengths $\ell \in [\text{len}(\text{link}(u)) + 1, \, \text{len}(u)]$.
2. Sweep the **left endpoint** $l$ backward from $N$ down to $1$ (symmetric to sweeping $r$ from $1$ to $N$ on $\text{SAM}(S)$!). At step $l$, call `access(pos[l])` on $\mathcal{T}_{\text{ST}}(S)$ to set the **leftmost starting position** $\text{first}_l(u) = l$ for all ancestors $u$ of the suffix leaf $\text{pos}[l]$.
3. For a fixed left endpoint $l = l_q$ and any node $u \in \mathcal{T}_{\text{ST}}(S)$ with current leftmost starting position $s = \text{first}_{l_q}(u) \ge l_q$, how many of $u$'s substrings ($\ell \in [\text{len}(\text{link}(u)) + 1, \text{len}(u)]$) fit inside $[l_q, r_q]$?
   A substring of length $\ell$ starting at $s$ ends at $s + \ell - 1 \le r_q \iff \ell \le r_q - s + 1$. Thus the number of valid substrings in node $u$ for query $(l_q, r_q)$ is:
   $$\text{cnt}(u; l_q, r_q) \;=\; \max\Bigl(0, \;\; \min\bigl(\text{len}(u), \, r_q - \text{first}_{l_q}(u) + 1\bigr) - \text{len}(\text{link}(u))\Bigr)!$$
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 3 — Algorithmic & Data-Structure Assembly"}
1. Order the nodes of $\mathcal{T}_{\text{ST}}(S) \cong \mathcal{T}_{\text{link}}(\text{SAM}(S^R))$ in **lexicographical DFS preorder** $\text{dfn}[1..2N-1]$ (sorting child edges of $\mathcal{T}_{\text{ST}}(S)$ by their first character $S[\text{pos}(v) + \text{len}(u)]$).
2. In this DFS order, the $K_q$-th lexicographically smallest distinct substring in $S[l_q..r_q]$ lies in the **first node $u$ in DFS preorder** where the prefix sum $\sum_{\text{dfn}[v] \le \text{dfn}[u]} \text{cnt}(v; l_q, r_q) \ge K_q$.
3. During the LCT `access(pos[l])` sweep as $l = N \dots 1$, each solid chain $C$ that changes $\text{first}_l(u)$ from $s_{\text{old}}$ to $l$ is a vertical path on $\mathcal{T}_{\text{ST}}(S)$, or equivalently on $\text{SAM}(S)$ via **Heavy-Path Decomposition on the SAM DAG (`noshi91` DAG-HLD)**: every root-to-state path on the SAM DAG crosses at most $O(\log N)$ light DAG edges, allowing binary search along heavy DAG paths coupled with LCT last-occurrence range counts in $O(\log^2 N)$ time per query.
::::

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Complete Derivation, Complexity Proof & Reference Solution — CP-III-05"}

- **Problem Source & Decoy Cluster**: Universal Cup / QOJ — *Range $K$-th Distinct Substring of $S[l..r]$* (`W2A-44` / `noshi91` Paradigm, Decoy Triad I · Part 2).
- **Target Chapter & Technique ID**: **[Chapter 11](../chapters/ch11-dynamic-sam-lct-stratification.qmd) & [Chapter 13](../chapters/ch13-virtual-suffix-trees-dominant-pairs.qmd) (`T-2A-04` / `T-2B-02`: Suffix-Tree Lexicographical Preorder + LCT `access` Color-Chain Sweep)**.
- **Unifying LCT Color-Chain Telescoping with Lexicographical DFS Preorder**:
  1. Build the Suffix Tree $\mathcal{T}_{\text{ST}}(S) \cong \mathcal{T}_{\text{link}}(\text{SAM}(S^R))$. Sort the children of each node $u \in \mathcal{T}_{\text{ST}}(S)$ alphabetically by the first character of their edge label $S[\text{pos}(v) + \text{len}(u)]$, and assign each node $u$ its alphabetical preorder index $\text{dfn}[u] \in \{1, \dots, V\}$.
  2. By construction, reading the strings of each node $u$ in increasing order of length $\ell \in [\text{len}(\text{link}(u)) + 1, \text{len}(u)]$ in increasing order of $\text{dfn}[u] = 1, 2, \dots, V$ enumerates **all distinct substrings of $S$ in exact lexicographical order**!
  3. Now sweep the left endpoint $l$ from $N$ down to $1$ using `Ch 11`'s LCT `access(pos[l])` on $\mathcal{T}_{\text{ST}}(S)$. At step $l$, each node $u$ has leftmost starting position $s_u = \text{first}_l(u) \ge l$, so its $\text{len}(u) - \text{len}(\text{link}(u))$ strings have leftmost ending positions in the contiguous interval:
     $$E_l(u) = \bigl[s_u + \text{len}(\text{link}(u)), \;\; s_u + \text{len}(u) - 1\bigr].$$
     For a query $(l_q, r_q, K_q)$ at $l = l_q$, a string in $u$ occurs inside $S[l_q..r_q]$ iff its leftmost ending position is $\le r_q$.

  4. **How to Find the $K_q$-th Substring in Alphabetical Preorder**:
     - **Method A (HLD Top-Down Walk on $\mathcal{T}_{\text{ST}}(S)$)**: Because LCT `access(pos[l])` updates $O(\log N)$ vertical solid chains per step $l$, and each vertical chain partitions into $O(\log N)$ HLD heavy-path segments, maintain for each node $u$ the sum of active substrings in its subtree (updating light-child subtree sums at the top of each heavy chain during `access`). To answer $(l_q, r_q, K_q)$, walk down $\mathcal{T}_{\text{ST}}(S)$ from the root: at the current heavy chain, binary search the deepest node where the subtree prefix sum reaches $K_q$, then step into the alphabetical child whose subtree contains the $K_q$-th element!
     - **Method B (DAG Heavy-Path Decomposition on $\text{SAM}(S)$, `noshi91`)**: Equivalently, on $\text{SAM}(S)$, decompose the transition DAG into heavy edges $u \to v^*$ maximizing $\text{dpsize}[v^*]$; every root-to-state path crosses at most $O(\log N)$ light DAG edges.
- **Boundary Pitfall Audit**:
  - **Ordering Children of $\mathcal{T}_{\text{link}}(\text{SAM}(S^R))$ Arbitrarily**: Only when children of $u$ in $\mathcal{T}_{\text{link}}(\text{SAM}(S^R))$ are sorted by the branching character $S[\text{startpos}(v) + \text{len}(u)]$ does preorder DFS match lexicographical order!
- **Complexity**: $O((N + Q) \log^2 N)$ time and $O(N \log N)$ space.
::::

### Problem `CP-III-06` — Asymmetric-Tie Cyclic Shift Dominance Counting

> **Statement**: You are given two strings $S[1..N]$ and $T[1..N]$ of lowercase English letters, each of length $N$ ($1 \le N \le 2 \times 10^5$).
>
> For each $i \in \{0, 1, \dots, N-1\}$, let $S^{(i)} = S[i+1..N] \cdot S[1..i]$ denote the $i$-th cyclic left shift of $S$, and similarly let $T^{(j)} = T[j+1..N] \cdot T[1..j]$ denote the $j$-th cyclic left shift of $T$.
>
> Count the number of ordered pairs $(i, j) \in \{0, 1, \dots, N-1\}^2$ such that $S^{(i)}$ is lexicographically **less than or equal to** $T^{(j)}$ ($S^{(i)} \le_{\text{lex}} T^{(j)}$).
>
> **Constraints**: $1 \le N \le 2 \times 10^5$, $|\Sigma| = 26$, time limit $2.0\text{ s}$, memory limit $1024\text{ MB}$.

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Decoy Elimination"}
- **Decoy Elimination**: This is *not* a multi-string GSAM problem (`Ch 09`), because GSAM merges substrings by right-context equivalence rather than sorting fixed-length $N$ cyclic rotations with tie-breaking. Instead, it is a cyclic suffix-sorting problem (`Ch 12`).
- **Diagnostic Signal**: If we concatenate $S \cdot S$ and $T \cdot T$, then $S^{(i)}$ is the length-$N$ prefix of the suffix starting at index $i + 1$ in $S \cdot S$, and $T^{(j)}$ is the length-$N$ prefix of the suffix starting at index $j + 1$ in $T \cdot T$. What goes wrong if $S^{(i)} = T^{(j)}$ (they match on all $N$ characters) and we simply compare their full suffixes in $S \cdot S \# T \cdot T \$$ using arbitrary separators?
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 2 — Combinatorial Word Invariant"}
**Asymmetric Sentinel Tie-Breaking**: Suppose $S^{(i)} = T^{(j)}$. Since $S^{(i)} = T^{(j)}$ has length $N$, repeating it twice gives $(S^{(i)})^2 = (T^{(j)})^2$ of length $2N$. Thus $(S \cdot S)[i+1 .. 2N]$ (of length $2N - i$) and $(T \cdot T)[j+1 .. 2N]$ (of length $2N - j$) are **both prefixes of $(S^{(i)})^2$**!
Consequently, the shorter of the two suffixes (at index $\max(i, j)$) will hit the separator character right after $S \cdot S$ (or right after $T \cdot T$) **while the other suffix is still reading characters of $S$ or $T$ in $[\texttt{'a'}, \texttt{'z'}]$**!
How should we choose the separator $c_1$ after $S \cdot S$ and the separator $c_2$ after $T \cdot T$ so that **whenever $S^{(i)} = T^{(j)}$**, the suffix from $S \cdot S$ is **guaranteed to sort strictly before** the suffix from $T \cdot T$ for **every** pair of indices $(i, j) \in \{1, \dots, N\}^2$?
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 3 — Algorithmic & Data-Structure Assembly"}
1. Construct the single string $U$ of length $4N + 2$:
   $$U \;=\; S \cdot S \cdot c_{\min} \cdot T \cdot T \cdot c_{\max},$$
   where $c_{\min} = \texttt{'a'} - 1$ (strictly **smaller** than every character in $\Sigma$) and $c_{\max} = \texttt{'z'} + 1$ (strictly **larger** than every character in $\Sigma$)!

2. Verify both tie cases when $S^{(i)} = T^{(j)}$ ($1 \le i, j \le N$):
   - If $i \ge j$, the suffix starting at $i$ in $S \cdot S$ hits $c_{\min}$ at offset $2N - i$ while the suffix starting at $j$ in $T \cdot T$ is at either a character in $[\texttt{'a'}, \texttt{'z'}]$ (if $i > j$) or at $c_{\max}$ (if $i = j$). Since $c_{\min} < \texttt{'a'} < \texttt{'z'} < c_{\max}$, $\text{suf}_U(i) < \text{suf}_U(2N + 1 + j)$!
   - If $i < j$, the suffix starting at $j$ in $T \cdot T$ hits $c_{\max}$ at offset $2N - j$ while the suffix starting at $i$ in $S \cdot S$ is at a character in $[\texttt{'a'}, \texttt{'z'}]$. Since $\texttt{'z'} < c_{\max}$, again $\text{suf}_U(i) < \text{suf}_U(2N + 1 + j)$!
3. Run linear-time `SA-IS` (`Ch 12`) on $U$ (appending a terminal sentinel $\$_0 < c_{\min}$ at index $4N + 3$) and count all inversions/pairs where an index $p \in [1, N]$ precedes an index $q \in [2N + 2, 3N + 1]$ in $\text{SA}_U$.
::::

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Complete Derivation, Complexity Proof & Reference Solution — CP-III-06"}

- **Problem Source**: AtCoder Beginner Contest 272 F — *Two Strings* (`W2B-09`).
- **Target Chapter & Technique ID**: **[Chapter 12](../chapters/ch12-sais-induced-sorting-lcp.qmd) (`T-2B-01`: Linear-Time Induced Suffix Sorting `SA-IS` with Asymmetric Sentinel Tie-Breaking)**.
- **Proof of Exact Equivalence ($\text{suf}_U(i) < \text{suf}_U(2N + 1 + j) \iff S^{(i)} \le_{\text{lex}} T^{(j)}$)**:
  For any $i, j \in \{1, \dots, N\}$:

  - **Case 1 ($S^{(i)} \ne T^{(j)}$)**: Their first mismatch occurs at some offset $t \in [0, N - 1]$. Since both $U[i .. i + N - 1] = S^{(i)}$ and $U[2N + 1 + j .. 3N + j] = T^{(j)}$ lie completely inside $S \cdot S$ and $T \cdot T$ without touching $c_{\min}$ or $c_{\max}$, the comparison between $\text{suf}_U(i)$ and $\text{suf}_U(2N + 1 + j)$ is decided at offset $t < N$ purely by $S^{(i)} <_{\text{lex}} T^{(j)}$.
  - **Case 2 ($S^{(i)} = T^{(j)}$)**: Let $W = S^{(i)} = T^{(j)}$. Then $U[i .. 2N]$ is the prefix of $W^2$ of length $2N - i + 1$ followed immediately by $c_{\min}$, while $U[2N + 1 + j .. 4N + 1]$ is the prefix of $W^2$ of length $2N - j + 1$ followed immediately by $c_{\max}$. Thus the two suffixes agree up to offset $t_0 = \min(2N - i + 1, 2N - j + 1) \ge N + 1$. At offset $t_0$, either the first suffix reads $c_{\min} < \Sigma$ or the second suffix reads $c_{\max} > \Sigma$ (or both if $i = j$). In every subcase, $\text{suf}_U(i) < \text{suf}_U(2N + 1 + j)$!
- **Boundary Pitfall Audit**:
  - **Using Two Small Sentinels $\#_1 < \#_2 < \texttt{'a'}$**: This is a classic contest bug! If you place $\#_1 < \texttt{'a'}$ after $S \cdot S$ and $\#_2 < \texttt{'a'}$ after $T \cdot T$, then when $S^{(i)} = T^{(j)}$ with $i < j$, the suffix in $T \cdot T$ is *shorter* ($2N - j < 2N - i$) and hits $\#_2 < \texttt{'a'}$ while $S \cdot S$ is still reading a letter $\ge \texttt{'a'}$, sorting $\text{suf}_U(2N + 1 + j) < \text{suf}_U(i)$ and missing the valid pair $(i, j)$! You **must** sandwich $\Sigma$ between $c_{\min} < \min\Sigma$ and $c_{\max} > \max\Sigma$.
- **Complexity**: $O(N)$ time and $O(N)$ space via `SA-IS`.
::::

### Problem `CP-III-07` — Range Bi-Colored Longest Common Substring

> **Statement**: You are given a string $S[1..N]$ of lowercase letters ($2 \le N \le 2 \times 10^5$) together with a binary color array $c[1..N]$ where $c[i] \in \{0, 1\}$ for each position $i \in \{1, \dots, N\}$.
>
> You must answer $Q$ queries ($1 \le Q \le 2 \times 10^5$). Each query specifies an interval $[l_q, r_q]$ ($1 \le l_q < r_q \le N$) and asks for the maximum length $L$ of a substring $w$ that occurs at least once inside $S[l_q..r_q]$ starting at a color-$0$ index $a$ ($l_q \le a \le r_q - L + 1, c[a] = 0$) **and** at least once inside $S[l_q..r_q]$ starting at a color-$1$ index $b$ ($l_q \le b \le r_q - L + 1, c[b] = 1$). Equivalently, compute:
> $$\text{Ans}(l_q, r_q) \;=\; \max_{\substack{l_q \le a, b \le r_q \\ c[a] \ne c[b]}} \min\Bigl(r_q - \max(a, b) + 1, \;\; \text{LCP}\bigl(S[a..N], S[b..N]\bigr)\Bigr),$$
> or output `0` if all indices in $[l_q, r_q]$ have the same color.
>
> **Constraints**: $2 \le N, Q \le 2 \times 10^5$, $|\Sigma| = 26$, time limit $2.5\text{ s}$, memory limit $512\text{ MB}$.

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Decoy Elimination"}
- **Decoy Elimination (Decoy Triad I)**:
  - Why not `Ch 10` (Persistent $\text{endpos}$ Merge)? There is no external pattern $T$ or single fixed locus $S[c..d]$ to query.
  - Why not `Ch 11` (LCT `access` Color-Chain Sweep)? LCT `access` maintains the rightmost occurrence $\text{last}_r(u)$ of all substrings, or the second-largest occurrence $e_2(u, r)$ when all indices are uncolored; here we require an opposite-color pair $(a, b)$ with $c[a] \ne c[b]$ inside $[l_q, r_q]$!
- **Diagnostic Signal**: We are maximizing a function of $\text{LCP}(S[a..N], S[b..N])$ and the interval $[\min(a, b), \max(a, b)] \subseteq [l_q, r_q]$ over all $\Theta(N^2)$ opposite-color pairs $(a, b)$. This is the exact signature of **Suffix-Tree Dominant Pairs (`Ch 13`, `T-2B-03`)**!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 2 — Combinatorial Word Invariant"}
**Bi-Colored Predecessor/Successor Dominance**: Build the Min-Cartesian Tree of $\text{height}[2..N]$ ($\cong \mathcal{T}_{\text{ST}}(S)$, `Ch 13`) and traverse it bottom-up using **DSU-on-Tree (`树上启发式合并`)**. At each internal node $u$ (of string depth $\ell_u = \text{height}[u]$), maintain two ordered sets of original string starting indices in $u$'s subtree: $\mathcal{S}_0(u)$ (for indices with $c[x] = 0$) and $\mathcal{S}_1(u)$ (for indices with $c[x] = 1$).

When inserting a light-child index $x$ of color $c[x] \in \{0, 1\}$ into $u$'s heavy sets, look up in the **opposite-color set** $\mathcal{S}_{1 - c[x]}(u)$:

- The largest element $x^- < x$ (producing the ordered pair $(x^-, x, \ell_u)$), and
- The smallest element $x^+ > x$ (producing the ordered pair $(x, x^+, \ell_u)$).

Why do these at most $2N \log_2 N$ bi-colored triples $(i, j, \ell_u)$ ($i < j, c[i] \ne c[j]$) dominate all $\Theta(N^2)$ opposite-color pairs for every query $[l_q, r_q]$? Because any other opposite-color element $z < x^-$ in $\mathcal{S}_{1 - c[x]}(u)$ has the exact same $\text{LCP} = \ell_u$, yet $[x^-, x] \subsetneq [z, x]$ and both have the same right index $x$, so $\min(r_q - x + 1, \ell_u)$ is identical! Symmetrically, any $w > x^+$ has $[x, x^+] \subsetneq [x, w]$ and $r_q - x^+ + 1 > r_q - w + 1$, so $(x, x^+, \ell_u)$ dominates $(x, w, \ell_u)$ in **both** interval containment and right-clipped length!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 3 — Algorithmic & Data-Structure Assembly"}
1. Build `SA`, `rk`, `height[2..N]` in $O(N)$ (`Ch 12`), construct the Min-Cartesian Tree of `height[2..N]`, and run DSU-on-Tree with two `std::set<int>`s ($\mathcal{S}_0, \mathcal{S}_1$) to extract the $\le 2N \log_2 N$ dominant triples $(i, j, \ell)$ ($i < j, c[i] \ne c[j]$).
2. For a query $[l_q, r_q]$, a triple $(i, j, \ell)$ is valid if $i \ge l_q$ and $j \le r_q$, contributing $\min(r_q - j + 1, \ell)$.
3. Apply the **Two-Threshold 2D Sweep (`Ch 13` §4)** by sweeping $l$ from $N$ down to $1$ and activating each triple $(i, j, \ell)$ when $l = i$:
   - **Regime 1 (Unclipped: $i \ge l_q$ and $j + \ell - 1 \le r_q$)**: Contributes $\ell$. Update a Prefix-Max Fenwick Tree `BIT_A` at index $p = j + \ell - 1$ with value $\ell$, and query `BIT_A.query_prefix(r_q)`.
   - **Regime 2 (Right-Clipped: $i \ge l_q$ and $j \le r_q \le j + \ell - 2$)**: Contributes $r_q - j + 1$. Update a Segment Tree `Seg_B` over right endpoints $r \in [1, N]$ with a range `chmax` of $-j$ on $[j, \min(N, j + \ell - 2)]$, and query $r_q + \text{Seg\_B.point\_query}(r_q) + 1$ in $O(\log N)$ time!
::::

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Complete Derivation, Complexity Proof & Reference Solution — CP-III-07"}

- **Problem Source & Decoy Cluster**: `[JSOI2016] 独特的基因` / Bi-Colored Substring Range Variant (`W2A-31`, Decoy Triad I · Part 3).
- **Target Chapter & Technique ID**: **[Chapter 13](../chapters/ch13-virtual-suffix-trees-dominant-pairs.qmd) (`T-2B-03`: Suffix-Tree DSU-on-Tree Dominant Pairs & Two-Threshold 2D Sweep)**.
- **Why $\le 2N \log_2 N$ Bi-Colored Dominant Triples Suffice**:
  Let $(a, b)$ be any opposite-color pair with $l_q \le a < b \le r_q$ and $c[a] \ne c[b]$, and let $u = \text{LCA}(\text{rk}[a], \text{rk}[b])$ in the Min-Cartesian Tree of `height[2..N]` have depth $\ell_u = \text{LCP}(S[a..N], S[b..N])$. During DSU-on-Tree at node $u$, one of $\{a, b\}$ belongs to a light child subtree of $u$ and is inserted into $\mathcal{S}_0(u) \cup \mathcal{S}_1(u)$ after the heavy child (and any earlier light children) are already present:

  - Suppose $b$ is inserted while $a$ is already in $\mathcal{S}_{c[a]}(u)$. Then the predecessor $b^- = \max\{z \in \mathcal{S}_{c[a]}(u) \mid z < b\}$ satisfies $l_q \le a \le b^- < b \le r_q$, so the emitted triple $(b^-, b, \ell_u)$ is valid for $[l_q, r_q]$ and achieves the exact same value $\min(r_q - b + 1, \ell_u)$ as $(a, b)$!
  - Suppose $a$ is inserted while $b$ is already in $\mathcal{S}_{c[b]}(u)$. Then the successor $a^+ = \min\{w \in \mathcal{S}_{c[b]}(u) \mid w > a\}$ satisfies $l_q \le a < a^+ \le b \le r_q$, so the emitted triple $(a, a^+, \ell_u)$ is valid for $[l_q, r_q]$ and achieves $\min(r_q - a^+ + 1, \ell_u) \ge \min(r_q - b + 1, \ell_u)$!
- **Two-Threshold 2D Sweep Without 3D Constraints**:
  Sort all dominant triples $(i, j, \ell)$ and queries $(l_q, r_q)$ by left endpoint $i, l_q$ descending ($N \to 1$):

  1. **Regime 1 ($j + \ell - 1 \le r_q$)**: Maintain a Prefix-Max Fenwick Tree `BIT_A` indexed by $p = j + \ell - 1 \in [1, N]$. When triple $(i, j, \ell)$ is activated at $l = i$, update `BIT_A.chmax(j + l - 1, l)`. For query $(l_q, r_q)$, `BIT_A.query_prefix(r_q)` gives the maximum unclipped $\ell$.
  2. **Regime 2 ($j \le r_q < j + \ell - 1$)**: Notice that the condition $j \le r_q \le j + \ell - 2$ is simply a **contiguous interval of query right endpoints $r_q \in [j, \min(N, j + \ell - 2)]$**! Maintain a Segment Tree `Seg_B` over $r \in [1, N]$ supporting range `chmax` with $-j$ and point query at $r_q$. When triple $(i, j, \ell)$ is activated at $l = i$ (and $\ell \ge 2$), apply `Seg_B.range_chmax(j, min(N, j + l - 2), -j)`. For query $(l_q, r_q)$, the best clipped length is $r_q + \text{Seg\_B.point\_query}(r_q) + 1$!
- **Boundary Pitfall Audit**:
  - **Omitting Regime 2 ($j \le r_q < j + \ell - 1$)**: When the global $\text{LCP}$ $\ell$ of $(i, j)$ extends past $r_q$ ($j + \ell - 1 > r_q$), the valid common prefix inside $S[l_q..r_q]$ is clipped to $r_q - j + 1$. Dropping Regime 2 misses all repeats whose full match crosses the right query boundary $r_q$.
- **Complexity**: $O(N \log^2 N + Q \log N)$ time and $O(N \log N)$ space.
::::

### Problem `CP-III-08` — Online Encrypted Front-Insertion Distinct Substrings & Suffix LCP

> **Statement**: Maintain a dynamic string $S$ over an integer alphabet $\Sigma = \{1, \dots, 10^9\}$, initially empty ($S = \varepsilon$). You must process $Q$ **online encrypted** operations ($1 \le Q \le 2 \times 10^5$). Let $\text{last\_ans} \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$ be the answer to the most recent query (initially $\text{last\_ans} = 0$). At step $k$ ($1 \le k \le Q$), let $n$ be the current length of $S$, and let $\text{suf}(i)$ ($1 \le i \le n$) denote the suffix of $S$ of length $i$ (so $\text{suf}(n)$ is the entire current string $S$, and $\text{suf}(1)$ is its last character). Each operation is one of three types:
>
> 1. `1 x`: Decode character $c = x \oplus (\text{last\_ans} \bmod 10^9)$ and **prepend** $c$ to the **front** of $S$ ($S \leftarrow c \cdot S$, increasing the length of $S$ to $n + 1$, where the new full string is $\text{suf}(n + 1) = c \cdot \text{suf}(n)$). Output the new total number of **distinct** non-empty substrings of $S$, and update $\text{last\_ans}$ to this count.
> 2. `2`: Delete the **front** character of $S$ (removing $\text{suf}(n)$ so the length of $S$ returns to $n - 1$). Output the updated number of distinct non-empty substrings of $S$, and update $\text{last\_ans}$ to this count.
> 3. `3 u v`: Decode $i = 1 + ((u \oplus \text{last\_ans}) \bmod n)$ and $j = 1 + ((v \oplus \text{last\_ans}) \bmod n)$. Output $\text{LCP}(\text{suf}(i), \text{suf}(j))$, and update $\text{last\_ans}$ to this value.
>
> **Constraints**: $1 \le Q \le 2 \times 10^5$, $c \in [1, 10^9]$, time limit $2.0\text{ s}$, memory limit $256\text{ MB}$. Because operations are online encrypted, **your algorithm must be strictly online and deterministic (zero randomized hashing)**.

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Decoy Elimination"}
- **Decoy Elimination (Decoy Triad II)**:
  - Why not offline SA + doubly-linked list on $S^R$? The input is **online encrypted** (`x ^ last_ans`) and includes `pop_front()` deletions (which create a dynamic version path!).
  - Why not standard online SAM (`Ch 09` / `Ch 11`)? Standard SAM `extend(c)` appends to the **right** (`push_back`), whereas here characters are prepended and popped at the **left** (`push_front` / `pop_front`), and Type 3 queries ask for $\text{LCP}(\text{suf}(i), \text{suf}(j))$ of two suffixes directly!
- **Diagnostic Signal**: Prepending a character $c$ to the front of $S$ adds **exactly one new suffix** $\text{suf}(n + 1) = c \cdot \text{suf}(n)$ while leaving all existing suffixes $\text{suf}(1), \dots, \text{suf}(n)$ and their pairwise lexicographical order **100% unchanged**! Which Part III structure maintains the sorted Suffix Array and adjacent `height` values dynamically under `push_front` and `pop_front` in $O(\log N)$ deterministic time with **zero hashing**?
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 2 — Combinatorial Word Invariant"}
**64-Bit Scapegoat Tags & Hash-Free BST LCP Recurrence**: Maintain all active suffixes $\text{suf}(1), \dots, \text{suf}(n)$ in an $\alpha = 0.75$ **Scapegoat Suffix Balanced Tree (`后缀平衡树`, `Ch 14` `T-2B-06`)**:

1. **Dietz–Sleator 64-Bit Tag Comparison in $O(1)$**: Each BST node $u$ covering tag range $[L_{\text{tag}}, R_{\text{tag}}] \subseteq [0, 2^{62}]$ is assigned midpoint tag $\text{tag}[u] = (L_{\text{tag}} + R_{\text{tag}}) / 2$ (with $\text{tag}[0] = 0$). Comparing the newly prepended suffix $\text{suf}(n) = c \cdot \text{suf}(n - 1)$ against any existing BST node $u$ (`suf(u) = S[u] . suf(u - 1)`) takes **$O(1)$ time** via the tuple comparison:
   $$\text{suf}(n) < \text{suf}(u) \iff \bigl(c, \, \text{tag}[n - 1]\bigr) < \bigl(S[u], \, \text{tag}[u - 1]\bigr)!$$

2. **Hash-Free Combinatorial BST LCP Bootstrapping**: Once $\text{suf}(n)$ is inserted into the BST between its inorder predecessor $n^-$ and inorder successor $n^+$, how do we compute $h_{\text{left}} = \text{LCP}(\text{suf}(n^-), \text{suf}(n))$ and $h_{\text{right}} = \text{LCP}(\text{suf}(n), \text{suf}(n^+))$ **without hashing**? By peeling the first character:
   $$\text{LCP}\bigl(\text{suf}(n), \text{suf}(u)\bigr) \;=\; \begin{cases} 0 & \text{if } S[n] \ne S[u], \\ 1 + \text{LCP}\bigl(\text{suf}(n - 1), \text{suf}(u - 1)\bigr) & \text{if } S[n] = S[u], \end{cases}$$
   where $\text{LCP}(\text{suf}(n - 1), \text{suf}(u - 1))$ is answered in $O(\log n)$ time as a **BST range-minimum query** over the adjacent `height` values stored inside the Suffix Balanced Tree itself!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 3 — Algorithmic & Data-Structure Assembly"}
1. At each node $u$ of the Scapegoat Suffix Balanced Tree, store:
   - `ch[u][0..1]`, `sz[u]`, `tag[u]` (`uint64_t` in $[0, 2^{62}]$);
   - `h[u]` $= \text{LCP}(\text{pred}(u), u)$ (the adjacent LCP with $u$'s inorder predecessor);
   - `min_h[u]` $= \min$ of `h[v]` over all nodes $v$ in $u$'s BST subtree (`pushup(u)`).
2. **Answering $\text{LCP}(\text{suf}(i), \text{suf}(j))$ via BST RMQ**:
   - If $i = j$, return $i$ (since $|\text{suf}(i)| = i$).
   - Swap $i, j$ if $\text{tag}[i] > \text{tag}[j]$. Walk down the BST from the root to find $\text{lca}_{\text{bst}}(i, j)$, then aggregate `h[v]` and right/left child `min_h` along the paths to $i$ and $j$ to get $\min_{\text{tag}[i] < \text{tag}[v] \le \text{tag}[j]} h[v]$ in $O(\log n)$ time!
3. **Handling `push_front(c)` (new suffix $n$)**:
   - Insert $n$ into the Scapegoat Tree using `(S[n], tag[n-1]) < (S[u], tag[u-1])`.
   - Find its inorder predecessor $n^-$ and successor $n^+$. Compute $h[n] = \text{LCP}(n^-, n)$ and updated $h[n^+] = \text{LCP}(n, n^+)$ via the Hash-Free BST LCP Recurrence, updating `min_h` along their root paths (and rebuilding the highest $\alpha$-unbalanced ancestor if needed).
   - Update distinct substring count:
     $$\text{distinct\_cnt} \mathrel{+}= n - \max\bigl(\text{LCP}(n^-, n), \, \text{LCP}(n, n^+)\bigr).$$

4. **Handling `pop_front()` (deleting suffix $n$)**:
   - Subtract $n - \max(\text{LCP}(n^-, n), \text{LCP}(n, n^+))$ from $\text{distinct\_cnt}$, restore $h[n^+] \leftarrow \text{LCP}(n^-, n^+)$ (which equals $\min(h_{\text{old}}[n], h_{\text{old}}[n^+])$!), and remove $n$ from the BST.
::::

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Complete Derivation, Complexity Proof & Reference Solution — CP-III-08"}

- **Problem Source & Decoy Cluster**: Online Encrypted Variant of `[SDOI2016] 生成魔咒` + `[BZOJ 3682] Phorni` (`W2B-10` / `W2B-36`, Decoy Triad II · Part 3).
- **Target Chapter & Technique ID**: **[Chapter 14](../chapters/ch14-cdawg-scdawg-suffix-balanced-trees.qmd) (`T-2B-06`: Hash-Free Scapegoat Suffix Balanced Tree with 64-Bit Midpoint Tags & BST RMQ LCP)**.
- **Proof of the Distinct Substring Delta Identity under `push_front` / `pop_front`**:
  When prepending $S[n] = c$ to create $\text{suf}(n)$ of length $n$, every new substring of $S$ is a **prefix** of $\text{suf}(n)$. A prefix of $\text{suf}(n)$ of length $\ell \in \{1, \dots, n\}$ already occurred in $S[1..n-1]$ iff it is a prefix of some existing suffix $\text{suf}(k)$ ($1 \le k < n$). By the LCP Interval Theorem, $\max_{1 \le k < n} \text{LCP}(\text{suf}(n), \text{suf}(k))$ is attained at either the immediate inorder predecessor $n^-$ or immediate inorder successor $n^+$ of $\text{suf}(n)$ in the Suffix Balanced Tree! Therefore, $\text{suf}(n)$ contributes **precisely**
  $$\Delta(n) \;=\; n - \max\bigl(\text{LCP}(\text{suf}(n^-), \text{suf}(n)), \; \text{LCP}(\text{suf}(n), \text{suf}(n^+))\bigr)$$
  new distinct substrings upon insertion, and removes the exact same $\Delta(n)$ upon `pop_front()`!

- **Non-Standard Reference Kernel (Hash-Free BST RMQ LCP & Scapegoat Insertion)**:

```cpp
// Assumes tag[1..n], h[1..n], min_h[1..n], ch[1..n][2] maintained in an alpha=0.75 Scapegoat BST
int query_bst_lcp(int x, int y) {
    if (!x || !y) return 0;
    if (x == y) return x;
    if (tag[x] > tag[y]) std::swap(x, y);
    int u = root;
    while (u) {
        if (tag[u] <= tag[x]) u = ch[u][1];
        else if (tag[u] > tag[y]) u = ch[u][0];
        else break; // u is the BST split node with tag[x] < tag[u] <= tag[y]
    }
    int ans = h[u];
    // Left walk from ch[u][0] to x: collect nodes strictly to the right of x
    for (int v = ch[u][0]; v; ) {
        if (tag[v] > tag[x]) {
            ans = std::min({ans, h[v], min_h[ch[v][1]]});
            v = ch[v][0];
        } else {
            v = ch[v][1];
        }
    }
    // Right walk from ch[u][1] to y: collect nodes <= y
    for (int v = ch[u][1]; v; ) {
        if (tag[v] <= tag[y]) {
            ans = std::min({ans, h[v], min_h[ch[v][0]]});
            v = ch[v][1];
        } else {
            v = ch[v][0];
        }
    }
    return ans;
}

int compute_adj_lcp(int x, int y) {
    if (!x || !y || S[x] != S[y]) return 0;
    return 1 + query_bst_lcp(x - 1, y - 1);
}
```

- **Boundary Pitfall Audit**:
  1. **IEEE-754 `double` Precision Underflow**: Using 53-bit `double` tags inside a randomized Treap causes tag collisions when tree depth exceeds $53$. An $\alpha = 0.75$ Scapegoat Tree with 64-bit unsigned integer bounds $[0, 2^{62}]$ guarantees depth $\le \log_{4/3}(2 \times 10^5) \approx 43 < 62$, making tag collisions mathematically impossible.
  2. **Order of `h[u]` Updates on Insertion**: When inserting $n$ between $n^-$ and $n^+$, you must first insert $n$ into the BST (so its structure is valid), compute $h[n] = \text{compute\_adj\_lcp}(n^-, n)$ and $h[n^+] = \text{compute\_adj\_lcp}(n, n^+)$ (which only query suffixes $\le n - 1$ whose `h` values are already finalized!), and then refresh `min_h` bottom-up along the root-to-$n$ and root-to-$n^+$ paths before triggering any Scapegoat subtree rebuild.
- **Complexity**: $O(Q \log Q)$ deterministic time and $O(Q)$ space, with zero hashing.
